questions.question: Women after women (a)/ spoke against the (b)/ practice of dowry, (c)/ No error (d)
questions.explanation: Should be 'Woman after woman spoke against...'.

questions.question: He was asking questions (a)/ after questions to ensure (b)/ if I was worthy of the post, (c)/ No error (d)
options: if I was worthy of the post,
questions.explanation: Should be 'asking question after question'.

questions.question: Village after village (a)/ have passed in the route but we (b)/ haven't reached our destination, (c)/ No Error (d)
options: have passed in the route but we
questions.explanation: 'Village after village' is singular, so the verb must be 'has passed'.

questions.question: He begs from (a)/ doors to doors so that (b)/ he may keep body and soul together, (c)/ No Error (d)
options: he may keep body and soul together,
questions.explanation: Correct form is 'door to door', both nouns singular.

questions.question: Piles on piles of books (a)/ was arranged (b)/ in the library, (c)/ No Error (d)
questions.explanation: Should be 'Pile on pile of books' — both nouns singular.

questions.question: There is a barrier among the egghead and (1)/ the hoipolloi and it would be lazy (2)/ idealism to ignore it. (3)/ No error (4)
options: There is a barrier among the egghead and
the hoipolloi and it would be lazy
questions.explanation: Two groups are compared, so 'between the egghead and the hoipolloi' is required.

questions.question: The main purpose of the visit (a)/ is to develop a close relationship (b)/ among the two countries, (c)/ no error (d)
options: The main purpose of the visit
is to develop a close relationship
questions.explanation: With two countries, use 'between the two countries'.

questions.question: These customs are (a)/ prevalent between the inhabitants of (b)/ the lower regions, (c)/ no error (d)
questions.explanation: 'Inhabitants' are more than two, so 'among the inhabitants' is correct.

questions.question: He was the fastest between all the contestants.
questions.explanation: 'All the contestants' are more than two, so 'amongst' replaces 'between'.

questions.question: There is an old rivalry between the three families for ages.
questions.explanation: Three families require 'among', not 'between'.

questions.question: Among you and me / she is quite rude / to the boy.
questions.explanation: With 'you and me' (two persons joined by 'and'), 'Between you and me' is correct.

questions.question: Ria's mother equally divided the chocolates among both her daughters.
questions.explanation: 'Both her daughters' refers to two, so 'between' is the correct preposition.

questions.question: Their father has left (a)/ behind a huge sum to be (b)/ distributed among the two brothers, (c)/ No error (d)
options: behind a huge sum to be
questions.explanation: Two brothers require 'between the two brothers'.

questions.question: If all of you quarrel (a)/ among yourself we shall not (b)/ be able to solve your problems, (c)/ No error (d)
options: be able to solve your problems,
questions.explanation: 'All of you' is plural, so the reflexive must be 'among yourselves'.

questions.question: The girl lay down / on the bed / besides her mother / and went to sleep.
questions.explanation: Physical position requires 'beside her mother' (by the side of).

questions.question: The river / flowed besides / the hillock / in our village.
questions.explanation: The river flowed by the side of the hillock, so 'flowed beside' is correct.

questions.question: Do you play / any other sports / beside of / cricket and football?
questions.explanation: The sense is 'in addition to', so 'besides' should be used, and never with 'of'.

questions.question: Besides the banyan tree / is the path / that leads to the forest.
questions.explanation: Position next to the tree requires 'Beside the banyan tree'.

questions.question: Beside the headline-making cases of mass shooters, (1)/ there are thousands of instances each year (2)/ in which police authorities try to get access to encrypted devices. (3)/ No Error (4)
options: Beside the headline-making cases of mass shooters,
there are thousands of instances each year
in which police authorities try to get access to encrypted devices.
questions.explanation: The meaning is 'in addition to', so 'Besides the headline-making cases' is correct.

questions.question: Most politicians predict (1)/ that the same members will (2)/ be elected despite of their failure to perform. (3)/ no error (4)
options: be elected despite of their failure to perform.
questions.explanation: 'Despite' is not followed by 'of'; use 'despite their failure' or 'in spite of their failure'.

questions.question: Despite of being a close friend he did not help me in any way.
questions.explanation: Correct form is 'Despite being' or 'In spite of being'.

questions.question: Science comprises of many (a)/ branches of (b)/ learning, (c)/ no error (d)
questions.explanation: 'Comprise' already includes 'of'; write 'Science comprises many branches' or 'consists of'.

questions.question: This question paper comprises (1)/ from questions on (2)/ general awareness and reasoning. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.explanation: 'Comprises' takes a direct object: 'comprises questions on...' — 'from' must be dropped.

questions.question: The students have been (a)/ awaiting for the results (b)/ for a long time. (c)/ No error (d)
questions.explanation: 'Await' is transitive: 'awaiting the results' or 'waiting for the results'.

questions.question: A few politicians were at enmity (1)/ with each other and no one was ready (2)/ to budge and this is what led to the division of the party. (3)/ No error (4)
options: A few politicians were at enmity
with each other and no one was ready
to budge and this is what led to the division of the party.
questions.explanation: 'A few politicians' are more than two, so 'with one another' is required.

questions.question: The five brothers (1)/ are at daggers drawn, (2)/ so they feel it below their dignity to talk to each other. (3)/ No Error (4)
options: so they feel it below their dignity to talk to each other.
questions.explanation: Five brothers are more than two, so 'to talk to one another' is correct.

questions.question: He was so afraid (1)/ that his knees (2)/ knocked one another. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.explanation: Knees are two, so 'knocked each other' is correct.

questions.question: I am yet to come across two people who are (1)/ so bent on making one another's (2)/ life as miserable as they can. (3)/ No error (4)
options: I am yet to come across two people who are
so bent on making one another's
life as miserable as they can.
questions.explanation: Two people require 'each other's life'.

questions.question: But the other candidates were often so busy fighting with each other that, again he went unscathed.
questions.explanation: 'The other candidates' are more than two, so 'fighting with one another' is correct.

questions.question: We must / take care / of one other / in times of crisis.
questions.explanation: 'One other' is not a valid reciprocal form; use 'of one another' (or 'of each other' for two).

questions.question: He, You and I (1)/ shall arrange everything (2)/ and shall not ask them for help. (3)/ No error (4)
options: and shall not ask them for help.
questions.explanation: For good news the order is 231 — 'You, he and I'.

questions.question: John, I and Hari have finished our studies. (a)/ (b)/ (c)/ No error (d)
questions.explanation: The first person pronoun should come last in good news: 'John, Hari and I'.

questions.question: You, he and she have done her best (a)/ in the interview and it is sure (b)/ that all of them will pass. (c)/ No error (d)
options: You, he and she have done her best
in the interview and it is sure
that all of them will pass.
questions.explanation: With a plural combined subject the possessive must be 'their best', not 'her best'.

questions.question: You and I have done (a)/ my best in (b)/ the examination (c)/ no error (d)
questions.explanation: 'You and I' takes the possessive 'our best', not 'my best'.

questions.question: I and my colleague have carefully considered (a) / the important issues raised by the report (b) which you sent me / and we have decided to take the following action. (c) / no error (d)
options: I and my colleague have carefully considered
the important issues raised by the report which you sent me
and we have decided to take the following action.
questions.explanation: Order of pronouns: the second person/third person should precede the first person – 'My colleague and I'.

questions.question: You, Mary and (A) me have (B) completed our work. (C) No error (D)
questions.explanation: As part of the subject the nominative 'I' is required, not 'me'.

questions.question: My sister and myself (1) / are pleased to accept (2) / your invitation to dinner. (3) / no error (4)
questions.explanation: The reflexive 'myself' cannot act as a subject; use 'My sister and I'.

questions.question: Madhuri and I have done my (1) / work patiently and diligently (2) / just for our safe and secure future. (3) / No Error (4)
options: Madhuri and I have done my
just for our safe and secure future.
questions.explanation: A plural subject 'Madhuri and I' needs the possessive 'our', not 'my'.

questions.question: Me and my friend have started working on a summer project which was approved by our teacher.
options: have started working on a summer project
questions.explanation: The subject requires the nominative case and correct order – 'My friend and I'.

questions.question: I and my wife (1) / were declared (2) / the best couple at the party (3) / No error (4)
options: the best couple at the party
questions.explanation: Correct order of pronouns: 'My wife and I'.

questions.question: I and Tina will (1) / go to the market (2) / in the evening. (3) / No error (4)
questions.explanation: Correct order of pronouns: 'Tina and I will'.

questions.question: Unless you do not (1) / take care of your health, (2) / you will continue to suffer (3). / No Error (4)
questions.explanation: 'Unless' is already negative, so 'do not' is redundant; write 'Unless you take care'.

questions.question: Until you do not (1) / go through your books (2) / you cannot get through the examination. (3) / No Error (4)
options: you cannot get through the examination.
questions.explanation: Double negative with 'Until'; it should be 'Unless you go through your books'.

questions.question: Until you do not go to the station (1) / to receive him (2) / I can hardly feel at ease. (3) / No Error (4)
options: Until you do not go to the station
I can hardly feel at ease.
questions.explanation: Remove the extra negative: 'Unless you go to the station'.

questions.question: If the Indian cricket team (a) / makes extra efforts, (b) / it will not be able to defeat the Sri Lankan team. (c) / no error (d)
options: it will not be able to defeat the Sri Lankan team.
questions.explanation: The sense demands 'Unless the Indian cricket team makes extra efforts' with a negative result clause; as written the logic is contradictory.

questions.question: One can never imagine / how hot it gets in Delhi / unless one doesn't go / there in person.
options: how hot it gets in Delhi
questions.explanation: 'Unless' already carries a negative, so 'doesn't' is wrong – 'unless one goes'.

questions.question: Ram cannot withdraw all his money unless he will give a prior notice.
questions.explanation: After 'unless' the present tense is used, not 'will' – 'unless he gives'.

questions.question: The condition of the healthcare (A) / system will not improve unless (B) / the committee does not recommend (C) / robust policy changes. (D) / No Error (E)
questions.explanation: Double negative after 'unless'; it should be 'the committee recommends'.

questions.question: Most disputes can be solved amicably unless one are not rigid.
questions.explanation: 'One' takes a singular verb and 'unless' needs no second negative – 'unless one is rigid'.

questions.question: Unless you do not give (A) / the keys to the safe (B) / you will be shot (C) / No error (D)
questions.explanation: Remove 'do not' after 'Unless' – 'Unless you give'.

questions.question: The temptation to exploit consumers (a) / usually prevails unless (b) / it is not curbed, (c) / no error (d)
questions.explanation: 'Unless' is negative in sense, so write 'it is curbed'.

questions.question: One should look for his (1) / own faults first (2) / and then for those of others (3). / No Error (4)
options: and then for those of others
questions.explanation: With the subject 'one', the possessive must be 'one's', not 'his'.

questions.question: One should respect (a) / religious beliefs of others, (b) / as much as his own. (c) / no error (d)
questions.explanation: 'his own' should be 'one's own' to agree with 'one'.

questions.question: One should study the history (a) / of his country because it alone can satisfy (b) / one's natural curiosity to know what happened in the past, (c) / no error (d)
options: of his country because it alone can satisfy
one's natural curiosity to know what happened in the past,
questions.explanation: 'his country' should be 'one's country' after the subject 'one'.

questions.question: One must (1) / obey ones (2) / teachers. (3) / No error (4)
questions.explanation: The possessive form needs an apostrophe: 'one's teachers'.

questions.question: One should have (1) / their teeth checked (2) / every six months. (3) / No error (4)
questions.explanation: 'their' must be replaced by 'one's' to match 'one'.

questions.question: One (1) / should keep (2) / his word. (3) / No Error (4)
questions.explanation: 'his word' should be 'one's word'.

questions.question: One should keep (a) / his promise (b) / if one wants respect from both friends and enemies, (c) / No error (d)
options: if one wants respect from both friends and enemies,
questions.explanation: 'his promise' should be 'one's promise'.

questions.question: I must say that everyone (a) / should respect (b) / one's teacher. (c) / No error (d)
questions.explanation: With 'everyone' the correct possessive is 'his/their teacher', not 'one's'.

questions.question: I don't want (a) / the blue pens. (b) / I want the red one's, (c) / no error (d)
questions.explanation: The plural substitute is 'ones' without an apostrophe – 'the red ones'.

questions.question: He was selected for the post (1) / because of he was familiar (2) / with both urban as well as rural way of life. (3) / no error (4)
options: He was selected for the post
with both urban as well as rural way of life.
questions.explanation: 'both' must be paired with 'and': 'both urban and rural'.

questions.question: It is not easy for an actor (a) / to earn respect from both, the fans (b) / as well as the critics, (c) / no error (d)
options: It is not easy for an actor
to earn respect from both, the fans
questions.explanation: 'both ... as well as' is wrong; use 'both the fans and the critics'.

questions.question: Between you and I, (1) / I am convinced (2) / that this painting by Neetu shows greater artistry than that of Reshma. (3) / No Error (4)
options: that this painting by Neetu shows greater artistry than that of Reshma.
questions.explanation: 'Between' is a preposition and takes the objective case – 'Between you and me'.

questions.question: Scientists show that there is a curious (1) / relationship among a lion's life span and (2) / the pattern of spots on each side of its face. (3) / No error (4)
options: Scientists show that there is a curious
relationship among a lion's life span and
the pattern of spots on each side of its face.
questions.explanation: Two things are compared, so 'among' should be 'between'.

questions.question: There is a barrier among the egghead and (1) / the hoipolloi and it would be lazy (2) / idealism to ignore it. (3) / No error (4)
options: There is a barrier among the egghead and
the hoipolloi and it would be lazy
questions.explanation: Only two groups are involved, so use 'between the egghead and the hoi polloi'.

questions.question: There was a (a) / comparison between (b) / you and he (c) / no error (d)
questions.explanation: After 'between' the objective case is required – 'you and him'.

questions.question: They had tried (a) / to win deceptively (b) / and this resulted in both failing or destroying others, (c) / No error (d)
options: and this resulted in both failing or destroying others,
questions.explanation: 'both' is correlated with 'and', not 'or' – 'both failing and destroying'.

questions.question: Both Renu as well as (a)/ her sister are very tall (b)/ and are in the basketball team, (c)/ No Error (d)
options: and are in the basketball team,
questions.explanation: With 'both' the correct correlative is 'and', not 'as well as'; it should be 'Both Renu and her sister'.

questions.question: After the examination is over, (1)/ you must hand over (2)/ both the answer booklets as well as the question paper (3)/ to the invigilator. (4)
options: both the answer booklets as well as the question paper
questions.explanation: 'Both ... as well as' is incorrect; use 'both the answer booklets and the question paper'.

questions.question: When it was time to (a)/ chose between staying or leaving the country (b)/, she choose to stay back. (c)/ no error (d)
options: chose between staying or leaving the country
questions.explanation: 'Choose between' takes 'and', not 'or', and the base form 'choose' is needed after 'to': 'to choose between staying and leaving'.

questions.question: He asked the same question (1)/ that why he was not selected (2)/ and everyone responded saying that he had failed. (3)/ No error (4)
options: that why he was not selected
and everyone responded saying that he had failed.
questions.explanation: 'That' must not precede the wh-word 'why'; it should be 'why he was not selected'.

questions.question: She does not understand (a)/ that how one can be employed as a stenographer (b)/ without the necessary qualification, (c)/ no error (d)
options: that how one can be employed as a stenographer
questions.explanation: Remove 'that' before the wh-word 'how'.

questions.question: He asked her that (1)/ whether she knew (2)/ what had happened last week when she was on leave. (3)/ No Error (4)
options: what had happened last week when she was on leave.
questions.explanation: 'That' cannot be used before 'whether'; it should be 'He asked her whether she knew...'.

questions.question: She asked her teacher / that if she could / explain that / problem again.
questions.explanation: Drop 'that' before 'if': 'She asked her teacher if she could explain that problem again.'

questions.question: Mohan's mother asked him / that if he had watered / all the plants in the morning. / No error
options: all the plants in the morning
questions.explanation: 'That' must be removed before 'if' in the reported question.

questions.question: Their is direct evidence that when learning (1)/ occurs, neuro-chemical communication between (2)/ neurons is facilitated and less input is required. (3)/ No error (4)
options: Their is direct evidence that when learning
neurons is facilitated and less input is required.
questions.explanation: The existential structure requires 'There is direct evidence', not the possessive 'Their'.

questions.question: "I had forgotten all such things just (1)/ for the sake of the greater good of everyone." (2)/ said there leader. (3)/ No error (4)
options: "I had forgotten all such things just
for the sake of the greater good of everyone."
questions.explanation: A possessive determiner is needed before 'leader': 'said their leader'.

questions.question: Why is it that they can develop only a (1)/ certain aspect of there life and not realize (2)/ their full potential? (3)/ No error (4)
options: Why is it that they can develop only a
certain aspect of there life and not realize
questions.explanation: 'There life' should be 'their life', the possessive form.

questions.question: They are cautious about their car as it's door is broken.
questions.explanation: Answer as given in the key; the possessive 'its' is required before 'door' rather than the contraction 'it's'.

questions.question: Such was the education / of the Spartans with regard to / one of the greatest of there kings.
options: one of the greatest of there kings.
of the Spartans with regard to
questions.explanation: 'There kings' should be 'their kings'.

questions.question: Citizens rarely know where or (1)/ how there city government spends (2)/ the money it collects by way of taxes (3)/. No error (4)
options: the money it collects by way of taxes
questions.explanation: 'There city government' should be 'their city government'.

questions.question: Her handwriting / is definitely / more beautiful / than your.
questions.explanation: Without a following noun the possessive pronoun 'yours' is required: 'than yours'.

questions.question: I am not sure / if the red car / in the parking slot / is your.
questions.explanation: Use 'is yours' as the possessive pronoun stands alone.

questions.question: I will never / judge you for / yours impromptu performance. / No error
questions.explanation: Before a noun the determiner 'your' is needed: 'your impromptu performance'.

questions.question: If you play / your cards right, / the job could be your / when she leaves.
questions.explanation: 'The job could be yours' — the standalone possessive pronoun is required.

questions.question: Seldom if ever (a)/ nature does operate (b)/ in closed and separate compartments, (c)/ no error (d)
questions.explanation: After the negative adverb 'seldom' the clause must be inverted: 'does nature operate'.

questions.question: Never I have listened to such beautiful music (a)/ as the piece we heard (b)/ on the radio last night, (c)/ no error (d)
options: Never I have listened to such beautiful music
questions.explanation: 'Never' at the start requires inversion: 'Never have I listened'.

questions.question: No sooner she had realised (a)/ her blunder than she began (b)/ to take corrective measures, (c)/ no error (d)
questions.explanation: 'No sooner' requires inversion: 'No sooner had she realised'.

questions.question: He is not an artist, (a)/ nor he is (b)/ a musician, (c)/ no error (d)
questions.explanation: After 'nor' the verb precedes the subject: 'nor is he'.

questions.question: If you practice (a)/ speaking English daily, (b)/ you will become fluent, (c)/ No Error (d)
questions.explanation: The verb form is 'practise'; 'practice' is the noun.

questions.question: The football team's practise (a)/ session was cancelled (b)/ due to heavy rain, (c)/ No Error (d)
questions.explanation: Here a noun is needed, so it should be 'practice session'.

questions.question: He gave me a piece of advise (a)/ regarding my career, (b)/ which I followed sincerely, (c)/ No Error (d)
options: He gave me a piece of advise
questions.explanation: 'A piece of advice' is required; 'advise' is the verb.

questions.question: The teacher adviced (a) / the students to revise their notes (b) / before the exam, (c) / No Error (d)
options: the students to revise their notes
questions.explanation: 'Advice' is the noun and 'advise' is the verb; the past tense of the verb is 'advised', so 'adviced' is wrong.

questions.question: The bad weather can (a) / effect the crops (b) / negatively, (c) / No Error (d)
questions.explanation: A verb is needed after 'can', so 'affect' (verb, to influence) should replace 'effect' (noun, result).

questions.question: The affect (a) / of the new policy was felt immediately (b) / by all the employees, (c) / No Error (d)
options: of the new policy was felt immediately
questions.explanation: After the article 'The' a noun is required, so 'effect' (result) must be used instead of the verb 'affect'.

questions.question: She lodged a complain (a) / against the noisy neighbors (b) / yesterday night, (c) / No Error (d)
questions.explanation: After 'a' a noun is needed, so it should be 'a complaint'; 'complain' is the verb.

questions.question: I complaint (a) / to the manager (b) / about the poor service, (c) / No Error (d)
questions.explanation: A verb is required here, so 'I complained' is correct; 'complaint' is a noun.

questions.question: After a long workout, (a) / I prefer to take a quick bathe (b) / to relax my muscles, (c) / No Error (d)
options: I prefer to take a quick bathe
questions.explanation: 'Bath' is the noun used with 'take a', while 'bathe' is the verb; correct form is 'take a quick bath'.

questions.question: I bathed (a) / the baby carefully (b) / after her nap. (c) / No Error (d)
questions.explanation: 'Bathed' is the correct past form of the verb 'bathe', so the sentence has no error.

questions.question: The baby was struggling to breath (a) / due to the cold weather, (b) / so we took her to the hospital, (c) / No Error (d)
options: The baby was struggling to breath
so we took her to the hospital
questions.explanation: After 'to' the verb 'breathe' is required; 'breath' is the noun.

questions.question: He took a deep breathe (a) / before starting his presentation, (b) / No Errors (c) / No Errors (d)
questions.explanation: With 'took a deep' the noun 'breath' is needed, not the verb 'breathe'.

questions.question: My driving license (a) / expired last month, (b) / and I haven't renewed it yet. (c) / No Error (d)
options: and I haven't renewed it yet.
questions.explanation: As a noun the correct spelling (British usage) is 'licence'; 'license' is the verb.

questions.question: He licenced (a) / the new software (b) / for commercial use. (c) / No Error (d)
questions.explanation: The verb is 'license', so the past form should be 'licensed', not 'licenced'.

questions.question: The knot was too lose (a) / and it came undone (b) / during the match, (c) / No Error (d)
questions.explanation: The adjective meaning 'not tight' is 'loose'; 'lose' is a verb meaning to be deprived of.

questions.question: The team was (a) / about to loose (b) / the match, (c) / No Error (d)
questions.explanation: After 'about to' the verb 'lose' is required, not the adjective 'loose'.

questions.question: Though the police tried all sorts of methods (a) / to illicit information (b) / from the public, they remained silent, (c) / No Error (d)
options: Though the police tried all sorts of methods
from the public, they remained silent
questions.explanation: The verb meaning 'to draw out information' is 'elicit'; 'illicit' is an adjective meaning illegal.

questions.question: His behavior was elicit (a) / and against company policies, (b) / No Errors (c) / No Error (d)
questions.explanation: An adjective is needed after 'was', so 'illicit' (unlawful) should replace the verb 'elicit'.

questions.question: He gave me all the information A)/ what I needed B)/ for the project. C)/ No error. D)
options: He gave me all the information
questions.explanation: 'Information' is an expressed antecedent, so the relative pronoun 'that' should be used instead of 'what'.

questions.question: This is the book A)/ what he was talking about B)/ during the meeting. C)/ No error. D)
questions.explanation: After the antecedent 'the book', 'that' must be used in place of 'what'.

questions.question: She told us about the challenges A)/ what she faced B)/ while travelling. C)/ No error. D)
options: She told us about the challenges
questions.explanation: 'The challenges' is the antecedent, so 'that she faced' is correct, not 'what she faced'.

questions.question: That I mean A)/ is not understood B)/ by the students. C)/ No error. D)
questions.explanation: There is no antecedent here, so 'What I mean' should be used instead of 'That I mean'.

questions.question: My neighbour's grandson / is only / five month old.
questions.explanation: The compound adjective of age takes the form 'five months old' (or 'five-month-old' before a noun).

questions.question: We bought / two dozens / mangoes from / the market.
questions.explanation: After a definite number, 'dozen' stays singular: 'two dozen mangoes'.

questions.question: Only five minutes time (a) / was allowed for each speaker (b) / during the function. (c) / No error (d)
questions.explanation: The possessive form is required: 'five minutes' time'.

questions.question: Balloons filled with helium travel hundreds or even thousands of miles.
questions.explanation: 'Hundreds' and 'thousands of' express indefinite numbers, which is the correct usage here.

questions.question: The judge decided that / the defendant was guilty of all charges, / and a five years punishment / in prison was appropriate.
options: the defendant was guilty of all charges,
questions.explanation: A numeral adjective before a noun stays singular and hyphenated: 'a five-year punishment', not 'a five years punishment'.

questions.question: I am thirty-two / year old and / my sister is fifteen.
questions.explanation: Without a hyphenated compound adjective before a noun, the plural is required: 'thirty-two years old'.

questions.question: Abhiram returned to the signal / and gave his last hundred rupees note / to the man / who had said he needed help.
options: who had said he needed help
and gave his last hundred rupees note
questions.explanation: As a compound adjective before 'note', it must be singular: 'hundred-rupee note'.

questions.question: Ten-miles distance (a) / is too long to cover (b) / on foot. (c) / No error (d)
questions.explanation: Correct form is 'Ten-mile distance' — the numeral adjective takes the singular noun.

questions.question: I am not sure / that the red car / in the parking slot / is yours.
questions.explanation: 'Not sure' expresses doubt/alternative, so 'whether/if' is required: 'I am not sure whether the red car...'.

questions.question: The manager said, "Could you please / confirm to me that you / have received all the items / that you had ordered?"
questions.explanation: The relative clause should be in the simple past to match the sequence: 'that you ordered'.

questions.question: He was doubtful that (a) / the man who had been run over (b) / by some vehicles had lain there for more than a day (c) / no error (d)
options: the man who had been run over
by some vehicles had lain there for more than a day
questions.explanation: 'Doubtful' takes 'whether/if', not 'that': 'He was doubtful whether...'.

questions.question: I don't know if any of the members (a) / of the party is conspiring (b) / against the President or not. (c) / no error (d)
options: I don't know if any of the members
questions.explanation: When the clause ends with 'or not', 'whether' must be used instead of 'if': 'I don't know whether any of the members...'.

questions.question: He asked me that I was (a) / preparing for the Civil service (b) / Examinations. (c) / no error (d)
options: He asked me that I was
questions.explanation: An indirect yes/no question after 'asked' takes 'if/whether', not 'that': 'He asked me if I was...'.

questions.question: The patient would not have died (a) / when the doctor had (b) / come on time. (c) / no error (d)
options: The patient would not have died
questions.explanation: A conditional sense is intended, so 'if' replaces 'when': 'if the doctor had come on time'.

questions.question: I cannot confirm (a) / you if he had paid (b) / the bill or returned the goods. (c) / no error (d)
options: the bill or returned the goods.
questions.explanation: With alternatives ('or'), 'whether' is required and 'confirm' does not take an indirect object: 'confirm whether he had paid'.

questions.question: Mr. Khan has a white (1)/ and a black dog (2)/ which guard his house from robbers. (3)/ No error (4)

questions.question: Gandhiji was a (1)/ philosopher and a (2)/ politician who served India (3)/ No Error (4)

questions.question: He does not like (1)/ this type of a man (2)/ who does nothing but find out fault with others. (3)/ No error (4)

questions.question: Don't talk to (1)/ her, she always (2)/ remain in temper these days. (3)/ No error (4)

questions.question: What sort of (1)/ the people are they (2)/ who always fight over worthless matters (3)/ No Error (4)

questions.question: He found himself (a)/ in a trouble (b)/ when he saw no rickshaw outside the station (c)/ No error, (d)

questions.question: In the conclusion (a)/ it may be safely asserted that (b)/ the poet preaches some moral implicity. (c)/ no error (d)

questions.question: The building's roof (a)/ needs repairing otherwise (b)/ it may fall down and result in many person's death, (c)/ no error (d)

questions.question: The Finance Minister (a)/ boasts of improving (b)/ the economic condition of the country's, (c)/ no error (d)

questions.question: The life of the rich (a)/ is not in many ways as peaceful (b)/ as that of the poor's, (c)/ no error (d)

questions.question: It is true that I met (a)/ the Chief Minister (b)/ at one of my friend's house, (c)/ no error (d)

questions.question: Her sister's-in-law (a)/ was attended (b)/ by all the members of the family, (c)/ no error (d)

questions.question: The followers of Hindu (a)/ crafted a gigantic temple in which (b)/ they could go inside and worshipped in the presence of God. (c)/ No error (d)

questions.question: Mrs. Varun not only stopped coming (a)/ here but also going to any place (b)/ which is related to her past tragedy. (c)/ no error (d)

here but also going to any place
which is related to her past tragedy.

questions.question: He not only comes (a)/ for shopping but also for (b)/ having a glimpse of the extremely beautiful sales girl. (c)/ no error (d)

questions.question: He is the most (a)/ intelligent and also (b)/ the very talented student of the college, (c)/ No error (d)

questions.question: The awkward tension between (1)/ Sam and I was, (2)/ as it turns out, completely one-sided. (3)/ No error (4)

questions.question: My boyfriend and me (1)/ went to the animal shelter, (2)/ and together we adopted a dog. (3)/ No error (4)

questions.question: The teacher instructed (1)/ the peon to let (2)/ the students and I go into the office of Principal. (3)/ No Error (4)

questions.question: You and myself (1)/ will enjoy the function (2)/ being arranged in honour of the new Principal. (3)/ No Error (4)

questions.question: She makes (a)/ her brother (b)/ to do his homework before dinner, (c)/ No Error, (d)

questions.question: The teacher let (a)/ the students (b)/ to leave early because of the heat, (c)/ No Error (d)

questions.question: I will have (a)/ the mechanic (b)/ checked the car today, (c)/ No Error, (d)

questions.question: They got (a)/ the electrician (b)/ to fix the wiring in the kitchen, (c)/ No Error, (d)

questions.question: We saw (a)/ him (b)/ to paint the fence yesterday, (c)/ No Error, (d)

questions.question: They had (a)/ the painter (b)/ to redecorate their living room, (c)/ No Error, (d)

questions.question: We made (a)/ them (b)/ to clean their room. (c)/ No Error, (d)

questions.question: She had (a)/ the dog (b)/ to groomed at the pet salon, (c)/ no error (d)

questions.question: He got (a)/ the landscaper (b)/ to mow the lawn on weekends, (c)/ No Error, (d)
options: to mow the lawn on weekends,
questions.explanation: Active 'get' correctly takes 'to + V1', so the sentence is right.

questions.question: One third of the birds (a)/ migrates from the southern (b)/ part of the country (c)/ No Error (d)

questions.question: Three fourths of the (a)/ pillar have (b)/ rotted away, (c)/ No Error (d)

questions.question: Sal trees have been (a)/ planted in nearly three fourth (b)/ of the forest area, (c)/ No Error (d)

questions.question: This sculpture is made from A)/ marble B)/ and is very detailed. C)/ No Error. D)
questions.explanation: Marble remains marble in the sculpture, so 'made of' is correct.

questions.question: The house is made from A)/ bricks B)/ and has a sturdy structure. C)/ No Error. D)
questions.explanation: The bricks do not change their nature, so 'made of' should be used.
